methods.label: Compare the two whole numbers
methods.explanation:
The two numbers have identical digits except in the ones place, so \(\overline{AMC12}\) is exactly \(2\) greater than \(\overline{AMC10}\). Removing that extra \(2\) from their sum leaves two copies of the smaller number. Thus
\[
\overline{AMC10}=\frac{123422-2}{2}=61710.
\]
Reading the corresponding digits gives \(A=6\), \(M=1\), and \(C=7\). The numbers are consequently \(61710\) and \(61712\), which have the required sum. Therefore
\[
A+M+C=6+1+7=\boxed{14},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Comparing decimal digits and recovering an equal share of an adjusted sum use elementary place value and arithmetic.
